clue.text: Old soldiers scared to get involved

indicators.note: letters that get involved with each other are mixed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Frightened veterans being drawn into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry of past centuries wore scarlet tunics and were nicknamed for them.

clue.text: Once erect I say my piece

indicators.note: what was once upright is no longer in that state, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A speaker who used to stand tall now has something to declare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once erect' suggests something fallen; the letters of ERECT plus I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to deliver a prepared passage or poem aloud, saying one's piece.

clue.text: Organise strike that will achieve aim unerringly

parts.note: to direct a show or project is to organise it
a hit is a blow or strike

explanation.surface: Someone planning a strike that will be bang on target.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot or missile landing squarely on its target is the perfect bullseye result.

clue.text: Done to a T — that's plain

parts.note: something done is finished or over

explanation.surface: Something completed perfectly is obvious for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done to a T' is an idiom for perfectly done, but here 'Done' gives OVER and 'to' just joins on the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not concealed.

clue.text: Tied up credit, we hear

indicators.note: signals that a word is spoken rather than written, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to give credit to someone is to trust or believe them

explanation.surface: A borrower's credit has been frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A trussed chicken or prisoner is bound tightly with string or rope.

clue.text: High level of service provided

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service
provided, as in 'on condition that', means if

explanation.surface: A church attended at a high level, on condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact mountain block, ground standing high above its surroundings.

clue.text: Awareness shown by military command

explanation.surface: Soldiers made alert by an order.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying heed means being alert to something; the drill order makes soldiers stand stiffly upright.

clue.text: Keep silent about mother's bankruptcy

indicators.note: the call for silence goes around, wrapping the word for mother

parts.note: sh is the call to keep silent
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A family keeping quiet about Mum's financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash is an old term for a financial collapse or business failure.

clue.text: Make a union defer tea break

indicators.note: these words are broken up and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Union officials postpone the tea interval.
explanation.definitionFit: To federate is to join separate states or bodies together in a league.

clue.text: A guard dog from hell?

parts.note: reads like a vicious watchdog, but means the three-headed beast that guards the underworld in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A complaint about a vicious watchdog.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the multi-headed hound keeps the gates of Hades.

clue.text: Bear right to enter London thoroughfare

indicators.note: the right letter goes into the word for bear

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A bear allowed to wander into a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: THE STRAND is a major street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Strand is a well-known road running from Trafalgar Square towards the City.

clue.text: Lot of grease going on bearing

indicators.note: the bearing is added on at the end of the grease

parts.note: fat is a greasy substance
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Plenty of oil being applied to a machine bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's destiny or fortune.

clue.text: Bound by discretion, one is silent

indicators.note: the numeral is tied up inside the word for discretion

parts.note: tact is discretion in dealing with others
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sworn to secrecy keeps quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being spoken, unvoiced.

clue.text: It slows a boat down, not by a fluke

definitions.text: It slows a boat down, not by a fluke

parts.words: It slows a boat down, not by a fluke
parts.note: a fluke seems to mean luck, but is also the barbed arm of a hook that grips the seabed, which this drogue lacks

explanation.surface: Something deliberately slows a boat, not by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue, a cone of canvas dragged in the water, holds a vessel steady without gripping the bottom.

clue.text: Disgraced bogus journalist

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A fake reporter has been exposed and disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humiliated publicly is made to feel ashamed and dishonoured.

clue.text: Girl crosses ravine to get plant

indicators.note: the girl's name stretches across, enclosing the ravine

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a chine is a deep narrow ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight

explanation.surface: A girl crosses a ravine to reach a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' is not greenery but industrial equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in the industrial sense means heavy equipment or the apparatus of a factory.

clue.text: A hole in ten unusually high

indicators.note: the hole goes inside the rearranged ten
the word ten is set out in an unusual order

parts.note: a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A golf hole that's unusually high, at ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges TEN into ENT, and 'in' puts MINE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means lofty or prominent, standing out above others.

clue.text: Sea walk to divert and please

indicators.note: to divert is to turn aside, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside promenade built to amuse and delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along the seafront is a long paved walkway beside the beach.

clue.text: One can't sleep through it

parts.note: reads like a noisy disturbance, but describes the condition of sleeplessness itself

explanation.surface: Complaint about a racket that keeps one awake.
explanation.definitionFit: The disorder is a chronic inability to fall or stay asleep.

clue.text: Marks the broken section

indicators.note: the word section is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Damaged parts bear marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to observe or note it, which is to take heed of it.

clue.text: So hard to get round part of London or New York

definitions.text: part of London or New York

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: So hard to get around a district of a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London known for nightlife, and SoHo is a Manhattan neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cities have a district by this name.

clue.text: Cover story with article inside

indicators.note: the article goes inside the word for story

parts.note: copy is newspaper text, a story
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A cover story that has an article tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning or overhead covering shelters what is below.

clue.text: Leave very little time to reduce the sentence

explanation.surface: A court gives a lighter sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave only a narrow margin is idiomatic; read literally, the phrase is to cut a penalty imposed by a court.

clue.text: Fed up with tea-break? Just the reverse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top
the word tea is broken up and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Fed up with tea breaks, someone asks for the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF, and 'break' rearranges TEA into EAT; 'reverse' is the definition, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or loss, especially in battle.

clue.text: Tell me if it's not up-to date and fashionable

parts.note: out of date things are said to be out
with it means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is behind the times or trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: An urging to speak up, demanding someone come clean.

clue.text: Project to cause confusion

explanation.surface: A project designed to confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to hurl or launch; to disconcert someone is also to put them off balance.

clue.text: Record start of the event

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: Logging the opening of the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a mark or record left behind, as on a graph.

clue.text: Maintain a high level

parts.note: reads like holding high standards, but means refilling a glass or tank to keep it full

explanation.surface: Advice to keep standards high.
explanation.definitionFit: Refilling something keeps it full to the brim.

clue.text: They tend to hurry back before the ship rounds the point

indicators.note: the reversed word comes before the rest
the word for hurry is read backwards

parts.note: to run is to hurry

indicators.note: the ship goes around the compass point

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Sailors tend to hurry back before their vessel rounds the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Carers in hospitals look after the sick; tend here is a verb.

clue.text: Girl's taking position as cashier

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, Diana shortened
a place is a position

explanation.surface: A girl takes up a post as a bank teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' is a verb: to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them, removing them from post.

clue.text: Constantly breaking the law, say

indicators.note: the words are broken apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who is forever flouting the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantly means at all times, forever.

clue.text: Make oneself useful and satisfy the wife

parts.note: to help is to make oneself useful
to meet a need or demand is to satisfy it

explanation.surface: A husband pitches in to keep his wife happy.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmeet is an old term for a supportive partner or spouse.
